Compare empirical bootstrap and fitted Student t simulations for a diversified seven-ETF portfolio.

## Scope

Results describe the supplied historical snapshot or a stated simulation. Model fit and scenario estimates are not evidence of performance on new observations. See the project README for the execution record and limitations.

```{r}
source("R/analytics_support.R")
set.seed(42)
```

```{r}
# Tickers for the seven ETFs chosen in portfolio specification
tickers <- c("VTI", "VEA", "VWO", "BND", "VNQ", "GLD", "QQQ")

# Portfolio weight on each ticker, matching the order above
weights <- c(0.35, 0.15, 0.10, 0.15, 0.10, 0.05, 0.10)

# Confirm weights sum to one
stopifnot(abs(sum(weights) - 1) < 1e-8)
```

```{r}
date_start <- "2020-01-01"        # first calendar date of the sample window
date_end   <- "2022-12-31"        # last calendar date of the sample window
ntickers   <- length(tickers)     # number of assets to loop over

for (i in 1:ntickers) {
  # Load adjusted price history for the requested ticker
  px  <- read_market_history(tickers[i], 
                    from = date_start, to = date_end)
  px  <- Ad(px)                              # keep the adjusted close column only
  ret <- na.omit(diff(px) / lag(px)) # daily discrete (simple) returns
  if (i == 1) {
    data <- ret                              # first ticker seeds the data object
  } else {
    data <- merge(data, ret)                 # later tickers are joined on by date
  }
}
names(data)      <- tickers        # label columns with their ticker symbols
data             <- na.omit(data)  # drop the leading NA row from the return calc
matret_discrete  <- as.matrix(data) # store aligned returns as a plain numeric matrix
head(data)
head(matret_discrete)
```

```{r}
# Daily discrete portfolio return: weighted average of the seven asset returns
portf.DiscreteRet <- weighted_returns(matret_discrete, weights, discrete = TRUE)
```

```{r}
# Compound $1 forward: running product of (1 + daily return)
portf.Index <- cumprod(1 + portf.DiscreteRet)

# Print the ending value
portf.Index[length(portf.Index)]
```

```{r}
ggplot(data.frame(date = index(data), value = as.numeric(portf.Index)),
       aes(x = date, y = value)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Portfolio Value ($)", title = "Growth of $1 Invested")
```

```{r}
# Convert daily discrete returns to daily log returns
portf.LogRet <- log(1 + portf.DiscreteRet)
```

```{r}
# Convert xts object to data frame for ggplot
df_plot <- data.frame(
  Date   = as.Date(index(data)),
  LogRet = as.numeric(portf.LogRet)
)

ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = Date, y = LogRet)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    title = "Log Returns of the Portfolio",
    x     = "",
    y     = "Daily Log Return"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title   = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.x = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)                  # fix the seed so draws are reproducible
num_paths       <- 5000        # number of simulated one year paths
trading_days    <- 252         # trading days in one simulated year
starting_wealth <- 100         # initial dollars invested in each path
```

```{r}
simulated_log_returns <- matrix(
  
  sample(
    as.numeric(portf.LogRet),          # pool of observed daily log returns
    size    = trading_days * num_paths, # total draws needed (252 x 5000)
    replace = TRUE                      # sample with replacement
  ),
  
  nrow = trading_days,   # rows = days within a single path
  ncol = num_paths       # columns = separate simulated paths
)
```

```{r}
# exp(log return) - 1 converts each log return back to a discrete return
simulated_discrete_returns <- exp(simulated_log_returns) - 1
```

```{r}
portfolio_values <- matrix(
  NA,                       # fill with NA; we overwrite row by row below
  nrow = trading_days + 1,  # one starting row plus one row per trading day
  ncol = num_paths          # one column per simulated path
)
```

```{r}
# Every path starts at $100
portfolio_values[1, ] <- starting_wealth
```

```{r}
for (i in 1:num_paths) {
  # For path i: grow $100 forward using the running product of (1 + daily return)
  portfolio_values[2:(trading_days + 1), i] <-
    portfolio_values[1, i] *
    cumprod(1 + simulated_discrete_returns[, i])
}
```

```{r}
# Grab the ending value of each path (last row of the portfolio value matrix)
terminal_wealth <- portfolio_values[trading_days + 1, ]

# 5th percentile of the 5,000 terminal values
var_5_boot <- quantile(
  terminal_wealth,   # distribution of ending values across all paths
  probs = 0.05       # the 5 percent lower tail cutoff
)

var_5_boot
```

```{r}
# CalcVaRES is a analysis utility function (defined in analytics_support.R).
# It takes a vector of terminal wealth values and a confidence level
# and returns both VaR and ES based on the 5 percent left tail.
boot_VaRES <- lower_tail_summary(terminal_wealth, 0.95)
boot_VaRES
```

```{r}
logret <- as.numeric(portf.LogRet)  # plain numeric vector for the moment functions

portf.mean  <- mean(logret)         # average daily log return
portf.sigma <- sd(logret)           # standard deviation of daily log returns
portf.skew  <- skewness(logret)     # skewness (0 = symmetric)
portf.kurt  <- kurtosis(logret)     # kurtosis (3 = Normal under Pearson convention)

portf.mean
portf.sigma
portf.skew
portf.kurt
```

```{r}
# Fit a Normal distribution to the daily log returns by MLE
n_fit <- fitdistr(logret, "normal")

# AIC = 2 * (number of parameters) - 2 * (log likelihood)
AIC_n <- 2 * length(n_fit$estimate) - 2 * n_fit$loglik
AIC_n
```

```{r}
# Fit a location-scale t distribution to the daily log returns by MLE
t_fit <- fitdistr(logret, "t", method = "L-BFGS-B", lower = c(-Inf, 1e-8, 1e-4),
                   control = list(parscale = c(sd(logret), sd(logret), 10), maxit = 2000))

# AIC = 2 * (number of parameters) - 2 * (log likelihood)
AIC_t <- 2 * length(t_fit$estimate) - 2 * t_fit$loglik
AIC_t
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)   # reproducible draw

# Extract the three fitted t parameters
m_hat  <- t_fit$estimate["m"]   # fitted location
s_hat  <- t_fit$estimate["s"]   # fitted scale
df_hat <- t_fit$estimate["df"]  # fitted degrees of freedom (controls tail weight)

# Draw daily log returns from the fitted t: location + scale * standard t draw
simulated_log_param <- matrix(
  m_hat + s_hat * rt(trading_days * num_paths, df = df_hat),
  nrow = trading_days,   # rows = days within a path
  ncol = num_paths       # columns = separate simulated paths
)

# Convert simulated log returns to discrete returns
simulated_discrete_param <- exp(simulated_log_param) - 1

# Build the portfolio value matrix the same way as the bootstrap
portfolio_values_param        <- matrix(NA, nrow = trading_days + 1, ncol = num_paths)
portfolio_values_param[1, ]   <- starting_wealth   # every path starts at $100

# Compound each path forward from $100
for (i in 1:num_paths) {
  portfolio_values_param[2:(trading_days + 1), i] <-
    portfolio_values_param[1, i] *
    cumprod(1 + simulated_discrete_param[, i])
}
```

```{r}
# Ending value of each parametric path
terminal_wealth_param <- portfolio_values_param[trading_days + 1, ]

# Use CalcVaRES on terminal wealth values at the 95% level
param_VaRES <- lower_tail_summary(terminal_wealth_param, 0.95)
param_VaRES
```

## Interpretation limits

Independent resampling does not preserve volatility clustering. Lower-tail summaries of terminal wealth are wealth thresholds, not loss VaR. Fitted t log-return simulations can produce extreme wealth values; inspect their tails before interpretation.
